instructions:
Write only `final_user`, a natural casual follow-up to
the frozen conversation prefix. It must ask the benchmark question faithfully
enough that its correct answer is unchanged, but it must not look like a test:
no answer options, test/exam/quiz language, answer key, or discussion of
evaluation. Make the question follow from the preceding topic or need. Do not
edit, repeat, or summarize the prefix. Aim for the supplied character budget;
natural coherence and semantic fidelity matter more than an exact count.

prefix.content: So my building just got fibre and I am trying to work out whether to keep the cable plan or switch to the 5g home internet box the carrier keeps mailing me about. I work from home four days a week and do a lot of video calls, and my partner streams most evenings. The price is nearly identical. What should I actually be comparing between the two before I decide
Compare upload speed and latency first, not just the advertised download number

Ok that helps. We also have a fair amount of stuff on the network, two laptops, a tv box, a couple of speakers and the doorbell camera that uploads constantly. Does having that many things connected change which option makes more sense
Yes, the doorbell camera makes upload speed the deciding factor here

prefix.content: I have been asked to automate our monthly reporting at work and I am not sure where to start. Right now three people copy numbers out of four systems into one spreadsheet and it eats most of a week. My manager wants it done by the autumn. Where would you begin with something like this
Fix the process on paper first, then automate it

That is fair, the process itself is a bit of a mess. Two of the four exports are already automated but one team still emails their numbers over as a pdf, and the fourth system has no export at all so someone reads it off the screen and retypes it. I was going to start with the pdf because it annoys everyone the most, but I suspect the screen reading one is where the real time goes. How would you prioritise those

Start where the time goes rather than where the annoyance is, but measure before you commit, because people are usually wrong about which step is slowest. Ask each of the three to note how long their part takes for one cycle. If the manual read really is the biggest block, find out whether that system has an interface or a scheduled report nobody told you about, since that is a far smaller job than scraping a screen. Keep the pdf one on the list, just second

prefix.content: Writing a story and need a Chinese answer to cowboys

The closest fit is probably the horsemen of the northern grasslands, who have the same outdoor working life and roughly the same place in the popular imagination. They come with a lot of cultural baggage though, so it depends how much of that you want your character carrying around with her
My character is from the south though, so the grassland riders do not really work

Then look at the river and canal trades instead of riders. Boat families in the south had the same rootless working life, moving goods and living on the water, and they turn up in fiction with a similar outsider feel. prefix.content: I have taken over the reporting at a small charity and the data situation is a mess. Donations sit in one online system, the membership list is a spreadsheet that three of us edit, gift aid claims live in a folder of scanned forms, and event attendance is written on paper and typed up later by whoever remembers. The trustees want a quarterly report pulling all of that together and at the moment I build it by hand over about four days. Small budget, no developer. Where should I start

Start by deciding what the quarterly report has to contain, because that tells you which of the four sources actually matter and you may find one of them does not. Then get everything into one place, even if that place is a single spreadsheet with one tab per source and a strict column layout. Do not buy a system yet. Once the layout is fixed and you have run one quarter through it by hand, you will know exactly what to ask a supplier for, and you will have a file to import

That makes sense. The membership spreadsheet is the worst of it, since the three of us all edit it and there are duplicate rows where somebody typed a name slightly differently. There is no id column, just names and email addresses, and some people have two addresses. Cleaning that by hand feels like a week of work I do not have. Is there a shortcut

Email is your best key, so start there rather than with names. Lowercase and trim every address, then flag any row where an address appears more than once, which handles most of the duplicates in one pass. For people with two addresses, keep both in separate columns and pick one as primary rather than trying to merge the rows straight away. Then add a proper id column of your own, numbers you assign once and never reuse, because that is what stops the problem coming back next year. Lock the sheet so only one of you edits while you do it

prefix.content: I have a spreadsheet where the dates are text like 03.04.2023 and none of the date functions will touch them. About four hundred rows of it. How do I fix that

Split the text on the full stops and rebuild it with a date function, taking the third piece as the year, the second as the month and the first as the day. Once the column is real dates you can format it however you like and the sorting will work properly too
Some rows have the year as two digits though, so that gives me nineteen twenty three on those ones

Wrap the year piece in a check on its length, and where it is two characters add two thousand to it. That works as long as none of your dates are from the last century, which for a working file they will not be. If you would rather not nest that much, do it as a helper column first and delete the column afterwards

prefix.content: My cousin asked what a quantity surveyor does and I froze

A quantity surveyor is the person on a building project who works out what everything will cost and then keeps track of whether it is actually costing that. They price the job before it starts, from the drawings and the specification, they measure what has been built as the work goes along so the right amounts get paid at the right time, and they handle the arguments about extra work and who pays for it when the design changes halfway through. They sit between the client and the contractor, and on a large job they are the reason anyone knows the project is in trouble before it is too late
That is still quite dense, can you make it simpler for me

Sure. A quantity surveyor is the money person on a building site. Before anything is built they work out what it should cost. While it is being built they check what has actually been done and make sure the builder is paid the right amount for it and no more. If the plans change and the job gets more expensive, they are the one who works out by how much and argues it out. Without them nobody would know whether the building was on budget until the end

It is grammatical but it is doing too much in one sentence, so a reader has to hold four things in their head at once to get to the end of it. Break it into two and put the purpose next to the interface each time. Something like this. The board has an M.2 B-Key slot for expansion. At 2242 it takes PCIe by four and SATA devices, and at 3052 it takes PCIe by one and USB 3.1 devices
Could be tighter than that

Then try this version. The board supports SSD and mobile module expansion through a single M.2 B-Key slot. The 2242 size connects over PCIe by four and SATA, while the 3052 size connects over PCIe by one and USB 3.1. That is two sentences, each doing one job, and it drops the repetition of compatible with
It still does not say clearly which of those is for the drive and which is for the mobile module

Fair, that is the actual problem rather than the length. This should fix it. The board takes both storage and mobile modules through one M.2 B-Key slot. Use the 2242 size for an SSD, which connects over PCIe by four or SATA. Use the 3052 size for a 4G or 5G module, which connects over PCIe by one or USB 3.1

It was typed wrong yes

prefix.content: What do people mean by the dogs in slang
It usually means somebody's feet
Give me some examples in actual sentences

Here are a few. I have been on my feet all day and now my dogs are barking, which means the speaker has been standing or walking a lot and their feet hurt. Let us go for a walk and give the dogs some exercise, meaning their own feet rather than any animal. I need new shoes, these ones are killing my dogs, meaning the shoes are causing pain. I danced for hours last night and now my dogs are sore, same idea again. In every case it works because the phrase sits somewhere it obviously cannot mean an animal, and that is what tells a listener how to read it
What about somebody playing with the dogs

That one goes the other way and reads as actual animals, because the slang sense does not survive being paired with a verb that only makes sense with a pet. Nobody hears playing with the dogs and thinks of feet. Compare it with the examples above, where the phrase turns up next to barking, sore, killing, exercise, all of which work for feet in a complaint about walking. The rule of thumb is that the slang sense only holds where the sentence is about discomfort or rest, and the moment the sentence is about interaction it flips back to the animal

prefix.content: Can you freeze cooked rice, one sentence answer please and nothing longer
Yes, as long as you cool it fast and reheat it once until piping hot
Can you freeze soft cheese, one sentence answer again please

You can, but the texture changes and it goes grainy when it thaws, so it is only worth doing if the cheese is going into something cooked afterwards rather than onto a plate. For a cheesecake or a sauce it is fine and nobody will know. Eaten on its own it is noticeably worse than it was, which is why most people who try it once do not bother again
Can you freeze double cream, one sentence again

Whipped it freezes well and holds its shape, but poured straight from the carton it separates when it thaws and looks curdled, so freeze it already whipped in small spoonfuls on a tray. Once they are solid they go in a bag together and you take out as many as you need. It is the same trick people use for leftover pesto and it works for the same reason

prefix.content: When were you made
I was built and released by my developer, in a version that came out fairly recently
Do you know everything from this year

No, and this is the part worth being clear about. What I know comes from text gathered up to a point in the past, so anything after that I will not have unless you tell me about it. I cannot look things up as we talk unless the tool is available, so treat me as reliable on what has been settled for a while and unreliable on anything recent
What about the year before that one

That one I am better on, though better is not the same as complete. The further back you go the more sources have accumulated and the more consistent they are, so my answers on older material are steadier. Anything close to the edge is thinner and often depends on a single source, which is exactly where I am most likely to sound confident and be wrong. If you have a specific area in mind, name it and I will tell you honestly how much I think I have on it rather than guessing at coverage in the abstract

prefix.content: Can you read text out of a picture

Not on my own in this setting, no. There are tools that pull text out of images and they work well on anything printed and reasonably straight, less well on handwriting and on photographs taken at an angle. If you have the text, paste it in and I can work with it directly
Do you understand emoji

Yes, they come through as characters like any other text, so I read them as part of the sentence rather than as pictures. They carry tone more than meaning most of the time, which is why the same one can soften a message or make it sarcastic depending on what sits around it. Where they get genuinely ambiguous is when somebody uses one as a substitute for a word, since the intended sense then depends on a shared joke I may not have
What is one, in plain terms

An emoji is a small picture used inside written text to carry tone or stand in for a word. They started on Japanese phones in the late nineties and spread everywhere once phones agreed on a common set, which is why the same character appears on every device even though it is drawn differently on each one. The word itself is Japanese and means picture character, and the resemblance to the English word emotion is a coincidence that has confused people ever since. In practice they do the job that a tone of voice does when you are speaking, which is why a message without one can read as colder than the sender intended

prefix.content: Two of us want to do a weekend of walking in September and I am the one organising it, which was a mistake. Neither of us has done more than a long day walk before, we both work full time so training is limited to weekends, and we would rather stay somewhere with a bed than carry a tent. Somewhere within about three hours of Manchester ideally. Where would you send us

The Yorkshire Dales suit that better than the Lake District for a first go, because the paths are gentler, the villages are close enough together to plan short days, and there are pubs with rooms at the end of most of them. Two days of ten to twelve miles each is a realistic first weekend without turning it into an ordeal you never repeat
That sounds about right. One of us has a dodgy knee on descents, which rules out anything with a long steep drop at the end of the day

Then plan the route so the climbing happens early and the last few miles are flat along a valley floor or a river path. Poles help more on the way down than the way up, and knees generally complain less when the descent is spread over distance rather than dropped in one go
Good, I will look at valley routes. What do we actually need to buy, given we own almost nothing

Boots are the only thing worth real money and they need wearing in before the trip, so buy them first and walk in them locally for a few weeks. After that, a waterproof jacket that is genuinely waterproof rather than showerproof, a small pack, and socks that are not cotton. Everything else you probably already own or can do without. Do not buy trousers that zip into shorts, do not buy a two hundred pound jacket for two days a year, and take a paper map even though both your phones have one on them

prefix.content: We are supposed to be moving to two week sprints at work and I have been handed the job of setting it up, which nobody asked me if I wanted. Team of six, mixed skills, currently working off a shared list that gets reordered whenever someone senior walks past. Where do I start with this
Start by fixing what the list is before you fix how often you plan it
The list is the problem, agreed. It has about eighty things on it, half of which nobody has looked at since last year, and three of them are entire projects rather than tasks
Then split the projects and archive anything untouched for six months

That got it down to about thirty, which already feels better. Next problem is that we finish about half of what we plan each fortnight and everyone has stopped believing the plan as a result. I am fairly sure the answer is to plan less, but if I turn up and say we are going to commit to half as much this sprint it is going to sound like I am asking the team to do less work, and one of the seniors will push back on that in front of everybody

Do not argue it in the abstract, bring the numbers. Work out what the team actually finished in each of the last four fortnights, put those four figures on a slide, and let the average do the talking. Then plan to that number rather than to what anybody hopes for. The pushback usually comes from a belief that the team is underperforming, and the honest answer is that the team delivers a consistent amount and the plan has been consistently wrong about it. That moves the conversation off effort and onto forecasting, which is far easier to win. Leave a little slack as well, because something always arrives mid sprint

prefix.content: Could you tidy this up for me. I am a visiting researcher at a university in Germany and my visa runs until the end of August this year. The university is extending my stay and I want to apply for an extension of the visa. Given that I am in Iran at the moment and will probably still be in Iran at the end of August, can I extend the visa from the German embassy here

I cannot tell you what the current rules are, since embassy procedures change and vary by country, so the answer to the substance of it has to come from the embassy itself. On the wording, here is a tidier version. I am a visiting researcher at a university in Germany and my visa is valid until the end of August this year. The university has extended my stay and I would like to apply for a visa extension. As I am currently in Iran and expect to remain here until the end of August, may I apply through the German embassy in Tehran

Can you do the same again but keep it closer to how I wrote it. I am a visiting researcher at a university in Germany and my visa runs until the end of August this year. The university is extending my stay and I want to apply for an extension of the visa. Given that I am in Iran at the moment and will probably still be in Iran at the end of August, can I extend the visa from the German embassy here

Here it is with the shape of your version kept. I am a visiting researcher at a university in Germany and my visa is valid until the end of August this year. The university is extending my stay, so I would like to apply for a visa extension. Since I am currently in Iran and will most likely still be here at the end of August, can I apply for the extension at the German embassy in Tehran. That keeps your order and your level of directness, and only tightens the tenses and the two places where the sentence ran on longer than it needed to

One more version please, a bit more formal this time, and it needs to work as the opening of an email to somebody I have never spoken to. I am a visiting scholar at a university in Germany and my visa is valid until the end of August this year. The university is extending my stay and I would like to apply for a visa extension. Can I do that at the German embassy in Tehran, since I am in Iran now and will probably be here until the end of August

This should work as an opening. I am writing as a visiting scholar at a university in Germany, where my current visa is valid until the end of August this year. My department has confirmed an extension to my stay and I would therefore like to apply to extend the visa accordingly. As I am presently in Iran and expect to remain here until the end of August, I would be grateful if you could confirm whether the application can be submitted at the embassy in Tehran, and what documents would be required. That opens with who you are and closes with a specific question, which is what makes it easy to answer

prefix.content: How do I make text bold in a plain text editor

It depends on where the text is going rather than on the editor. If the file is plain text, there is no bold at all, only characters, so the usual approach is to write it in a lightweight markup and let whatever displays it do the styling. The common convention is to put two asterisks either side of the words you want bold, or two underscores either side, and both are read the same way by most systems that understand it. If the text is going somewhere that does not understand any of that, the honest options are capitals or spacing, both of which are worse. Tell me where it is going and I can be more specific
It is going in a chat app

Then it depends which one, but most of them accept the asterisk convention, and a few use a single asterisk either side rather than two. The safest thing is to type it with the asterisks and look at what happens when it sends, since they all render as you type in the preview. If the app strips them out and leaves the words plain, it does not support it and there is nothing to be done short of using capitals, which reads as shouting
So two either side of the word

Two either side for the version that works most widely, and no spaces between the marks and the word, since a space between them is the usual reason it fails to take. The closing pair has to be there as well, or the whole rest of the line gets swallowed

prefix.content: Which is right, the cinema is at the left or on the left
On the left is the natural one in English
This morning a bus or the bus was late

Both work but they say different things. The bus was late means a particular bus that you and your listener already have in mind, usually the one you take every day. A bus was late means some bus, one of many, and it sounds like a report about traffic rather than about your morning. In practice, if you are explaining why you were late yourself, you want the bus, because the definite article is what signals that it is your usual one
Is Ankara a capital or the capital of Turkey
The capital, since there is only one

prefix.content: What would be a good title for a meeting with a senior colleague who is going to mentor me on applications
Try, mentoring session on applications, with her name and the date
Any others to pick from

A few, depending how formal the calendar is. Applications mentoring, first session. Guidance on applications with a senior colleague. Career conversation, applications. Or simply mentoring, part one, if the rest of the team can see your diary and you would rather not advertise what it is about. The plainest one usually ages best, since you will be looking at it in a list of thirty other entries in six months

I have three questions for her and they are worded badly. One, she did her masters later on in her career when she was already senior, so what made her feel it was needed at that point. Two, how did she get recognised as a fellow at that institution. Three, how have those things added value to her career. Could you rewrite them so they sound better

Here they are. One, you completed your masters at a point when you were already established in a senior role, so what led you to decide it was still worth doing then. Two, could you tell me how the fellowship came about and what the process involved. Three, looking back, what difference have those two things made to how your career developed since. Each one now asks about her experience rather than the fact itself, which is what gets a real answer

prefix.content: It is unbearable in this flat tonight

Top floor flats hold the heat long after the outside air has dropped, so opening one window does very little. Get a draught going by opening two on opposite sides of the place, and put a fan in front of the cooler one rather than pointing it at yourself
Only one side of it opens though

Then put the fan in the window facing outwards rather than in, which pushes the hot air out and pulls cooler air in under the doors. It feels backwards and works better than the obvious way round. Close the curtains on the sunny side during the day as well, since most of tomorrows heat arrives before noon
Will the fan run all night
Most of them will, and a cheap one costs very little to leave on. Put it on the lowest setting that still moves air, because the noise is what wakes people rather than the heat

As a highly motivated and experienced manager, I recently relocated from Thailand to the area and am excited to apply for opportunities to further my career in the retail industry. I am writing to express my interest in the customer host supervisor position available in your organisation. After reading the job description, I believe that my skills and experience perfectly align with the requirements for this role and that I would be able to make a contribution from the start

Here is a version that keeps everything and reads more smoothly. As an experienced and highly motivated manager, I have recently relocated from Thailand and am keen to take the next step in my retail career. I am writing to express my interest in the customer host supervisor position you have advertised. Having read the job description closely, I believe my skills and experience align well with what the role requires, and I am confident I could contribute from the start. The main changes are that the two paragraphs now hand over to each other rather than restarting, and the claim about alignment is softened from perfectly to well, which reads as more credible rather than less
Could you put it into one paragraph and drop the word experienced, it appears twice in the rest of the letter already

Here it is as one. Having recently relocated from Thailand, I am keen to take the next step in my retail career and am writing to express my interest in the customer host supervisor position you have advertised. Reading the job description, my background lines up closely with what the role requires, and I am confident I could contribute from the start. That is one paragraph, the repeated word is gone, and nothing has been lost from the original
Are you able to make the opening line hit a bit harder, it still sounds like every other letter they will get

Try this as the opening. Ten years of managing retail floors, most recently in Thailand, and I am now looking for the right team to do it with here. Then carry straight on into the interest in the role. Opening with the specific thing you have done is what separates it, since every other letter opens with a description of how motivated the writer is and none of them can be checked

prefix.content: How does this read as a reply to a supplier. All the samples arrived today and they are wonderful. I am excited to show them to our designer and see what she comes up with. We are definitely interested in the dies, the embossing folders, the cutting folder and the red rubber stamps as well
It reads warmly and it is clear, but it gives them nothing to act on, so expect a reply that just says thank you

Fair. Same message then, but ending with something they can actually do. All the samples arrived today and they are wonderful. I am excited to show them to our designer and see what she comes up with. We are definitely interested in the dies, the embossing folders, the cutting folder and the red rubber stamps as well

Then add a closing line that hands them the next step. Something like this. The samples arrived today and they are excellent. I am showing them to our designer this week and will come back with designs once we have talked them through. In the meantime we are interested in the dies, the embossing folders, the cutting folder and the red rubber stamps. That way they know when to expect you and what to keep in stock

Good. Now the full version with the timing and the quote request in it, and tell me whether it holds together or whether it is asking for too much at once. All the samples arrived today and they are wonderful. I am excited to show them to our designer and see what she comes up with. We are definitely interested in the dies, the embossing folders, the cutting folder and the red rubber stamps too. I hope to see her next week and we will get back to you soon with designs. Can you let me know what you would need in order to quote for some red rubber options

It holds together and it is not asking too much, since the quote request is the only actual ask and everything before it is context. One change worth making is to move the question to its own line at the end rather than leaving it attached to the sentence about designs, because a reader skimming on a phone will see the paragraph, register that you are pleased, and reply without noticing there was a question in it at all. Everything else can stay as it is

prefix.content: In this sentence, the junior developer married the senior engineer because she was pregnant, who is she
Grammatically it could be either, and most readers take it as the developer
How did you land on that reading though

Partly the structure and partly assumption, and it is worth separating those two. Structurally, the subject of the main clause is the natural antecedent for a pronoun in the reason clause that follows it, so the developer is the default reading. But the honest answer is that plenty of readers get there by assumption about which of the two roles a woman is more likely to hold, which is a different thing entirely and is not evidence about the sentence
The engineer is the nearer noun to she though, so why does proximity not win here, since that is the rule I was taught

Proximity is a tendency rather than a rule, and it loses to subject preference fairly often in English, which is why this sort of sentence is used to show that pronoun resolution is not mechanical. Readers weigh several things at once, the grammatical role of each candidate, how recently each was mentioned, and what they believe about the world. Here the first and third pull towards the developer while the second pulls towards the engineer, and the third does far more work than most readers would admit
